ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account for review of the false "I'm Here" tap + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 22:42:00 after accepting at 22:33:00, and a $6.61 cancellation fee was applied [F3][F6]. Because the driver is the cancelling party and he asserts the rider no-showed, the fee only stands if NS-1 is satisfied: the arrival confirmation, the position at that moment, and more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting at the pickup [NS-0][NS-1].

Both NS-1 conditions fail on the system record. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while 1000 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup after the tap [F5]; his closest approach at any time was 873 m and he never came within 200 m [F1]; the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all [F4]. GPS and timeline records override the driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12], and that statement is contradicted point-for-point by the stationary window 1000 m away [F2] and by the cancellation timeline [F3] [NS-1].

With NS-1 unmet, the fee has no basis and the $6.61 cancellation fee on the record must be returned in full to the rider — for this fixed-fare RydeX trip the whole disputed charge is that fee [F6][NS-2][NS-7]. The rider's own presence cannot be system-verified (only her message at 22:38 [F9]); that fact cuts both ways but is irrelevant, since the charge fails on the driver's arrival conditions, not on whether the rider showed up [NS-1].

Separately, because the driver pressed the arrival button while GPS placed him 1000 m from the pickup point, this is an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, which calls for the account review add-on under NS-2; the driver's profile (2 of 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 d) is context only and does not decide anything [F5][F17][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Acceptance and cancellation times with the fee on record [F3][F6] only show the fee was applied, not that it was earned; NS-0 routes a driver-side no-show allegation into NS-1, whose conditions fail [F1][F5] [NS-0][NS-1].

The five-minute stationary window [F2] was spent 1000 m from the pickup after a tap made 1000 m out with 0 s inside 200 m [F5], so neither NS-1 (ii) nor (iii) is met; the driver withdrew this framing.
The rider's message that she was at the pickup [F9] is a statement without a GPS record locating her, and it does not cure the driver's missing arrival conditions [F1][F5] [NS-1].

The profile figures [F17] cannot decide the merits or convert a failed arrival into an operational error; profile facts never decide an issue alone, and the account action rests on the tap itself [F5] [NS-2].
With no speed band and no incident on the route in the trip window [F13][F14], 1.8 mm of light rain [F15] is not a reasonable cause under RD-4 for standing 1000 m away [RD-4].

The flag_account request is granted only through the NS-2 add-on for the false arrival confirmation [F5], not through RD-6: RD-6 also requires the driver's profile route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the rider's profile shows route: 0 upheld [F17] [RD-6][NS-2].
